newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam TV soap opera to highlight AIDS danger.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam TV soap opera to highlight AIDS danger.

text.p: Vietnam said on Tuesday that a television drama series highlighting the dangers of AIDS and "other social evils" would be aired by the end of this year.
The official Vietnam News Agency (VNA) said the series, entitled "The Wind Blows Through Dark and Bright Areas", was a $1.2 million project funded by the European Union.
A group of Australian film makers has provided technical assistance since shooting of the soap opera began last year.

"The show is part of the country's combined efforts to fight the most deadly disease of the century," VNA said. "It will have around 30 episodes featuring life in the modern world, with all its day-to-day problems, designed to warn local people of HIV/AIDS and other social evils."
Social evils is a catch-all term which Hanoi uses to describe prostitution, pornography, drug abuse and gambling.

VNA said more 4,200 cases of human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infections had been reported since the communist country's first case was identified in 1990. It said 353 of those infected by HIV had developed the Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome (AIDS), more than half of whom have died.
Ho Chi Minh City, notorious during the Vietnam War as a den of pimps and prostitutes, is home to more than a third of Vietnam's known HIV cases and 200 AIDS sufferers.

Health workers say cultural taboos have long been a hindrance to tackling Vietnam's growing AIDS problem. Sex outside marriage is frowned upon, homosexuality is still widely regarded as a foreign phenomenon and sexual matters are rarely discussed in public.

However, the government has launched several campaigns to inform the public about HIV/AIDS prevention and a special cafe has even been opened in Ho Chi Minh City to dispense coffee, condoms and a telephone hotline for advice on safe sex.
"This subject, once regarded as taboo, is now included in (the) education curriculum, stressing a healthy and loyal family life as the key to people's happiness," VNA said.
